author: Andy Jassy
title: Amazon 2025 Letter to Shareholders
headline: Andy Jassy: AI is a once-in-a-lifetime shift, so Amazon spends about $200 billion in 2026 and accepts weaker free cash flow for now.
summary: Jassy frames 2025 around “inflections”: progress is never a straight line, so Amazon invents new ones, runs parallel bets and is willing to start over. Revenue grew 12% to $717 billion and operating income 17% to $80 billion, but free cash flow fell from $38 billion to $11 billion on AI spending. He rejects the bubble worry for Amazon: AWS’s AI revenue run rate passed $15 billion in Q1 2026, its own chips run above $20 billion a year, and customer commitments, including over $100 billion from OpenAI, cover a substantial portion of 2026 AWS capex. Robotics, drones, grocery and the Leo satellite network are the other bets.

takeaways.label: Move
takeaways.text: Amazon plans about $200 billion of capex in 2026, mostly for AI; much of the AWS share is already backed by customer commitments and should be billed in 2027 and 2028.

takeaways.label: View
takeaways.text: Is AI over-hyped, a bubble, or a poor return? For Amazon his answer is no, no, and yes: margins and returns on capital will be appealing.

takeaways.label: View
takeaways.text: Its own chips change the economics: Trainium2 beat comparable GPUs on price-performance by about 30%, Trainium3 is 30 to 40% better again, and at scale Trainium should save tens of billions of capex a year.

takeaways.label: Watch
takeaways.text: Amazon Leo, the satellite network with more than 200 satellites in orbit, launches in mid-2026; Delta will start with 500 planes in 2028.

takeaways.label: Watch
takeaways.text: AWS still turns away demand: it added 3.9 gigawatts of power in 2025 and expects to double total capacity by the end of 2027.

risks.text: While capex grows faster than revenue, free cash flow stays under pressure; servers are billed only 6 to 24 months after the cash goes out.
AI could change how people want to shop, so even Amazon’s most familiar retail experience may have to be rebuilt from scratch.

quotes.text: My strong conviction, at least for Amazon, is that the answers are no, no, and yes.
We’re not investing approximately $200 billion in capex in 2026 on a hunch.
Our chips business is on fire, changes the economics for AWS, and will be much larger than most think.

stocks.note: Revenue +12% to $717 billion in 2025; free cash flow down to $11 billion on AI capex.
A close partner, but AWS customers are moving inference to Amazon’s own Trainium chips.
Cloud CPUs ran almost only on Intel until Graviton, now used by 98% of the top 1,000 EC2 customers.
Chose Amazon Leo for in-flight Wi-Fi, starting with 500 planes in 2028.
